meta.title: An Email for Ms. Ong
meta.textType: functional: an email to a pen-pal teacher

paragraphs: On Friday, January twenty-ninth, Lily and May sat at Lily's desk in the evening. In December, Ms. Ong asked the Explorers, "What are you doing in January?" Now it was time to answer. Lily typed on the laptop, and May sat beside her with a notebook. Pip lay under the chair. The top of the screen said "To: Ms. Ong," "From: Lily and May," and "Subject: Our January." Lily typed, "Dear Ms. Ong, thank you for your question." "This is our answer for the Explorers."

May opened her notebook and read her list. It said "Ferry, January ninth," "Market, January twenty-third," "Bean jars," and "Coach Matt." There was also a drawing of a blue boat. Lily wrote a short sentence for each event. "On January ninth, the club took the blue ferry to Hill Pier." "On January twenty-third, we interviewed sellers at the market." "Our class also grew beans in jars, and now the plants are in the school garden." Lily typed, "Leo liked the market best, but I liked the ferry, because I could draw the river." "I liked the market, too," said May.

"Now we must tell about Coach Matt," said May. Lily typed, "Coach Matt is our football coach." "He was born in a small town by the sea." "He has worked at our school for six years." "Our topic for February is festivals." "What is your topic?" "Would you tell us about it, please?" "Here is the link to our blog." "Best wishes, Lily and May, for the Explorers." Lily pressed "Send." The word "Sent" appeared on the screen. Pip put his front paws on May's knee.

"What are we doing in February?" asked Lily. "We are preparing a festival quiz," said May. "We are collecting stories from our families, and Leo is drawing the posters." "Mia is taking the photos." "We will post the quiz on our blog, so it will be online for everybody." "On the final Thursday, some Explorers will perform a short play."

"Would you give Pip a biscuit, please?" asked Lily. May found a biscuit in her bag, and Pip ate it. "I think that Ms. Ong will be interested in our quiz," said May. "The quiz is an invitation to her class, too," said Lily. "This term is busy, but it is a happy one," said May. Now the girls waited for an answer. Pip lay down again under the chair.
